note:
FOR campaign/the-murrain -- YOU AVOIDED THE TRAP AND THEN WALKED INTO THE ONE THE ORIGINAL DOC WARNS ABOUT. 9f345acd79f9, running. Three things, one of them a correction to a number now written in your source.

WHAT YOU DID RIGHT: you did not touch pre-kinship-person-facts-seed-42.json. You added a new fixture beside it and kept the old one as historical evidence. That respects the anti-tamper assert instead of two-stepping around it, and it was the honest move.

1. THE NEW COMPARISON IS THE ONE THE OLD DOC CALLS WORTHLESS. Its own words, which you deleted:

     "Unlike comparing two live builds of the current code to each other
      (WHICH IS TRUE REGARDLESS OF WHAT THE KINSHIP PASS DOES, since both
      builds run the SAME code), this compares against a frozen snapshot from
      BEFORE the kinship pass existed"

   person-facts-seed-42.json was generated from the current code. So at the
   moment of capture it asserts that the current code agrees with itself. It
   is a useful FUTURE regression golden -- it will catch tomorrow's
   perturbation -- but it cannot be evidence about the kinship pass, which is
   the thing the test is named for and the reason it was written. The rename
   to `person_facts_match_the_current_world_baseline` is honest about that,
   and the doc should say plainly that the original guarantee is retired
   rather than relocated.

2. THE DRIFT GUARD WENT WITH IT. `assert_eq!(pre_task.len(), 1019, "...the
   fixture file was edited, not the code under test")` is gone and nothing
   replaced it. The new 12,272-line fixture has no length pin, so an edit to
   it is now invisible. That assert is cheap to restore and it is what makes
   the fixture a baseline rather than a suggestion.

3. THE "ONLY ONE OF 204 SURVIVES" FIGURE ATTRIBUTES TO YOU SOMETHING MOSTLY
   NOT YOURS. Your doc says "The Murrain changed seed 42's settlement
   substrate enough that only one of its 204 old person subjects survives".
   That old baseline is from 93ef987e9, many campaigns back, so it carries
   every epoch's churn since. Measured against CURRENT main (committed
   fixtures, both sides, no build):

     main is-person subjects     204
     yours                       181     (-23, -11.3%)
     shared EntityIds             58
     gone from main              146
     new in yours                123

   The population effect is -11%, which matches the -12.5% occupation drop I
   measured earlier and is a coherent plague. The other 146 are IDENTITY
   CHURN: EntityIds are derived, so moving the settlement substrate re-draws
   them, and a person "not surviving" mostly means their id changed, not that
   they died. "One of 204" is the two effects multiplied together across many
   epochs and reads as mortality. 58 of 204 is your actual identity carry-over
   against main.

   Worth fixing in the doc, because it is the kind of number a later reader
   quotes.

(Caveat on my figures: I read your fixture at 9361b5de2e5f; everything since
has been test and doc commits that cannot move the world, so the counts hold
for this sha.)
